items.prompt: A booking is created with status PENDING because its event type requires confirmation. What does the idempotency extension do on that create?
items.answer: No key is set, as only ACCEPTED creates get one
distractors: It sets a uuidv5 key from start, end and user id
It sets a random uuidv4 key for pending bookings
It rejects the create, as pending rows need a key
items.explanation: The create hook generates idempotencyKey only inside if (args.data.status === BookingStatus.ACCEPTED). A PENDING booking is passed to query(args) untouched, so the unique key does not guard unconfirmed bookings.

items.prompt: An ACCEPTED booking with an idempotency key is updated to status CANCELLED. What happens to its idempotencyKey?
items.answer: It is set to null, which frees that slot key again
distractors: It is kept, so the user can never rebook the slot
It is replaced with a new key that includes the cancel time
It is left alone; the extension only acts on create calls
items.explanation: The update hook sets args.data.idempotencyKey = null when the new status is CANCELLED or REJECTED. Because the key is derived from start, end and user id, nulling it lets a new ACCEPTED booking for the same slot get the same key without a unique-constraint clash.

items.prompt: SLOTS_CACHE_TTL is set to "abc". What TTL does withSlotsCache use when it stores a computed result?
items.answer: 2000 ms, since parseInt gives NaN and || falls back
distractors: 0 ms, so the slots result is never stored in Redis
It throws, because the env value is not a number
abc is handed to Redis, which then rejects the set
items.explanation: ttl = parseInt(process.env.SLOTS_CACHE_TTL ?? "", 10) || DEFAULT_SLOTS_CACHE_TTL. parseInt("abc") is NaN, which is falsy, so the default 2000 is used. The set itself is fire-and-forget.

items.prompt: Two getSchedule calls send the same fields, but one sends { eventTypeId, startTime } and the other { startTime, eventTypeId }. Do they share a slots cache entry?
items.answer: No, since JSON.stringify keeps keys in insertion order
distractors: Yes, as JSON.stringify sorts the object keys alphabetically
Yes, the cache key hashes the sorted field values
No, each request mixes a random nonce into its key
items.explanation: The cache key is JSON.stringify(args.input). JSON.stringify serializes properties in insertion order and does not sort them, so differently ordered but equal inputs produce different keys, which is the "key stability = property order" risk in the guide.

items.prompt: reserveSlot is called for a seated event type, and no ACCEPTED booking exists yet for that slot. What does the handler do?
items.answer: It writes no SelectedSlots row but still sets the uid cookie
distractors: It reserves one seat in SelectedSlots for this booker uid
It throws NOT_FOUND, since that slot has no booking at all yet
It reserves every seat so that no one else can grab them
items.explanation: For a seated event, shouldReserveSlot becomes false when there is no booking yet (and when seatsLeft < 1). The upsert block is skipped, but the code after it still serializes the uid cookie and returns { uid }.

items.prompt: reserveSlot is called with _isDryRun true for a free, non-seated slot. What is written to the database?
items.answer: Nothing; the upsert is skipped for dry runs
distractors: A SelectedSlots row with releaseAt of now
A SelectedSlots row flagged as a dry-run hold
A booking row with status PENDING for the slot
items.explanation: The write runs only if (eventType && shouldReserveSlot && !reservedBySomeoneElse && !_isDryRun). With _isDryRun true the upsert never runs; the lookup of other reservations is a read, and the cookie is still set.

items.prompt: handleCancelBooking is called for a booking whose status is already CANCELLED. What happens?
items.answer: It throws HttpError 400, already been cancelled
distractors: It returns success again, being idempotent
It deletes the calendar event a second time to be sure
It throws 404, since cancelled bookings are not loaded
items.explanation: The guard throws statusCode 400 "This booking has already been cancelled." The comment explains why: a booking can be CANCELLED by a reschedule, and a second cancel must not delete the calendar event the reschedule kept.

items.prompt: An event type has no cancellation-reason setting (null). An attendee who is not the host cancels without a reason, outside the platform. What happens?
items.answer: It proceeds, as by default only hosts must give a reason
distractors: It fails with 400, as a reason is always required by default
It fails with 401, because only hosts may cancel a booking
It proceeds, but only once the host has approved the request
items.explanation: isCancellationReasonRequired treats a null setting as MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY and returns isHost. For a non-host attendee that is false, so the reason check does not throw and cancellation continues.

items.prompt: Same default setting. A request with no session passes cancelledBy equal to the host's email and no reason. How is it treated?
items.answer: As the host, so it fails with 400 reason required
distractors: As an attendee, so the cancel just goes through as is
As unauthenticated, so it fails with a 401 error
As the host, so it skips every remaining check
items.explanation: isCancellationUserHost is bookingToDelete.userId === userId || bookingToDelete.user.email === cancelledBy. cancelledBy comes from the input, so matching the host email makes the caller count as host; with MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY a reason is then required, and its absence throws 400.

items.prompt: A signed-in user who is neither a host nor the owner cancels a seated-event booking without a seatReferenceUid. What does handleCancelBooking do?
items.answer: It throws HttpError 401, User not a host of this event
distractors: It cancels just that user's own seat in the booking
It cancels the whole booking for every attendee
It throws HttpError 403, Forbidden for this seat
items.explanation: For seatsPerTimeSlot events without a seatReferenceUid, the handler requires the caller to be one of eventType.hosts or the event type owner, else it throws statusCode 401 with "User not a host of this event". Cancelling one seat needs the seatReferenceUid.

items.prompt: A signed-in user who is not in team T calls a route behind eventOwnerProcedure for a team event of T, with no users list. What does the team permission check return?
items.answer: true, as the local PermissionCheckService is a stub
distractors: false, so the route throws FORBIDDEN for that user
It throws, since PBAC is not configured in the repo
false for every route except the delete route only
items.explanation: eventTypes/util.ts defines its own PermissionCheckService class whose checkPermission always returns true, so the team branch never throws. The guide flags this; it is the authorization boundary you can break.

items.prompt: A webhook subscription has no secret. What value does sendPayload put in the X-Cal-Signature-256 header?
distractors: An HMAC computed with an empty string key
No header at all for this delivery
A SHA-256 hash of the request body
items.explanation: createWebhookSignature returns the HMAC-SHA256 hex digest only when a secret exists; otherwise it returns "no-secret-provided". The header is always sent, so receivers must reject that value.

items.prompt: A visitor who is not signed in books through POST /api/book/event. What userId does the route pass in bookingMeta?
distractors: null, as the anonymous user id
0, the id of the system user
It rejects the request with a 401
items.explanation: Anonymous bookings are expected: getServerSession returns no user, and the route passes userId: session?.user?.id || -1 to RegularBookingService.createBooking.

items.front: List the main steps of creating a booking in cal.diy.
items.back: Booker mutation posts to /api/book/event; the route runs Turnstile (optional), bot detection and an IP-hash rate limit, then RegularBookingService parses the event-type-specific schema, runs blocked-email, spam and limit checks, dedupes, re-checks availability server-side, writes in a transaction (idempotency key on ACCEPTED), then fans out calendar, email and webhook work.

items.front: Where is the TOCTOU seam in reserveSlot?
items.back: findReservedByOthers reads whether someone else holds the slot, and only afterwards the handler upserts SelectedSlots rows, with no transaction or lock between the check and the write. Two bookers can both see the slot free and both reserve it.

A booking event gathers subscribers, schedules a Task (immediate or later) through the tasker; the processor takes a batch, runs the handler and marks it succeeded or retries with backoff (at-least-once). sendPayload POSTs the body with an X-Cal-Signature-256 HMAC and redirect: "manual".
